Walking in a straight line and riding a bicycle are the activities which are possible due to a part of the brain. Choose the correct location and name of this part from the given table:

items.stem: Read the Assertion (A) and Reason (R) given below and select the correct option.
items.assertion: Nerve impulse is a one way conduction.
items.reason: Nerve impulse is transmitted from dendrite to axon terminals.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.

items.answer: (c) Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false. Nerve impulses are always transmitted across a synapse from the axon terminals of one neuron to the dendrite/cell body of the next neuron but never in the reverse direction. Since the neurotransmitter is present only in the axon terminals and not in the dendrite or cell body, it cannot be released from the dendrite or cell body even if the impulse reaches there.

items.answer: (b) Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A). Both the statements are true. The nervous system is the system of conducting tissues that receives the stimulus and transmits it to other parts of the body, forming a network of nerves. It is involved in receiving information (sensation) and generating responses to that information (motor response). The units which make up the nervous system are called nerve cells or neurons. Nerve impulses are always transmitted across a synapse from the axon terminals of one neuron to the dendrite/cell body of the next neuron.

items.stem: Which part of the human brain is responsible for adjustment of movement and posture?
items.answer: The cerebellum of the hindbrain is responsible for adjustment of movement and posture.

items.stem: We suddenly withdraw our hand when a pin pricks. Name the type of response involved in this action.
items.answer: Reflex action.

items.stem: Which parts of the human brain are responsible for auditory reception and sensation of smell?
items.answer: The temporal lobe of the forebrain is responsible for auditory reception and the parietal lobe of the forebrain is responsible for the sensation of smell.

items.stem: Which part of the brain controls respiratory centre?
items.answer: The pons present in the hindbrain controls the respiratory centre.
items.ocr: Printed 'The pons present n the hindbrain'; missing 'i' restored.

items.stem: Name the part of hind brain which takes part in regulation of respiration.
items.answer: Pons.

items.stem: Name the part of the brain which controls the involuntary activities.
items.answer: Medulla oblongata.

items.stem: Mention the exact part of brain which controls the voluntary movements of muscles.
items.answer: The cerebellum controls the voluntary movements of muscles.

items.stem: A person under the influence of alcoholic drink walks clumsily. Which part of his brain is affected to show this condition?
items.answer: Cerebellum.

items.stem: You are walking in a dark room. Suddenly looking at something snake-like lying on the floor, you jumped on one side. What kind of action is this called?
items.answer: This is called a reflex action.

items.stem: Write the full form of CSF.
items.answer: The full form of CSF is cerebrospinal fluid.

items.stem: What is the full form of EEG?
items.answer: The full form of EEG is electroencephalograph.

items.stem: Which part of the human brain is responsible for intelligence and memory?
items.answer: The cerebrum of the forebrain is responsible for intelligence and memory.

items.stem: Name the stimuli to which plants respond.
items.answer: Plants respond to three stimuli, namely light, touch and gravitational force.

items.stem: How do control and coordination take place in plants?
items.answer: In plants, control and coordination take place with the help of plant hormones called phytohormones.

items.stem: List various phytohormones.
items.answer: Some of the phytohormones are: Auxins, Gibberellins, Cytokinins, Abscisic Acid (ABA) and Ethylene.
